clue.text: Artisan's skill for two parts of his boat

definitions.text: Artisan's skill for two parts of his boat

parts.words: Artisan's skill for two parts of his boat
parts.note: split into two words, the craftsman's skill reads as a boat that is convenient, an adjective plus a word for a vessel

explanation.surface: A craftsman's know-how is described as covering two sections of the vessel he owns.
explanation.walkthrough: Say it as two words, HANDY CRAFT: a 'handy' boat. The setter treats the two halves as two parts of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Handicraft is manual skill in making things, the trade of an artisan.

clue.text: Incisive sort of writer? Hardly

parts.note: a word meaning to cut roughly, so incisive in a literal way, but also a dull jobbing writer who is anything but sharp

explanation.surface: The speaker scoffs at the idea that a certain writer is incisive.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb for chopping roughly is 'incisive' in the cutting sense, while the writer it names is far from sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a jobbing writer of dull work, and to hack is to cut roughly.

clue.text: Darling pet, Zola's girl

definitions.meaning: the Newfoundland dog who is nursemaid to the Darling children in Peter Pan
title heroine of an Émile Zola novel, a courtesan

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is cherished, a young woman from a French novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' reads as an endearment but is the family name in J. M. Barrie's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are characters: the Darlings' dog nursemaid in Barrie's play, and the courtesan of Zola's novel.

clue.text: Measure of concern, rising due to inflation

definitions.text: Measure of concern, rising due to inflation

parts.words: Measure of concern, rising due to inflation
parts.note: concern hints at worry, but here it is financial interest, measured as a percentage that banks raise when prices climb

explanation.surface: Worry levels are said to climb as things swell up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concern' suggests worry; read it as the money charged on a loan, which central banks raise to fight inflation.
explanation.definitionFit: This percentage measures the charge on borrowed money and is typically raised to curb inflation.

clue.text: Name of famous archer killed by another

definitions.meaning: first name of the outlaw Hood of Sherwood Forest, a great bowman
in the nursery rhyme the Sparrow shoots Cock ... with his bow and arrow

explanation.surface: A celebrated bowman is said to have been shot by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Who killed Cock Robin?' has the Sparrow answer 'with my bow and arrow', so the bird was killed by another archer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Hood's first name, and the bird of the nursery rhyme shot dead by the Sparrow.

clue.text: No businessman's. duty bound to take part in it

definitions.text: No businessman's. duty bound to take part in it

parts.words: No businessman's. duty bound to take part in it
parts.note: duty bound seems to mean obliged, but read it as tied to customs duty: in this commerce no trader pays tariffs

explanation.surface: No trader is obliged to join in some activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty bound' means obliged, but here 'duty' is a customs tax: in this system traders pay no import tariffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce between countries without tariffs or quotas is free of customs duty.

clue.text: Some swordsmanship we see, in each case ending with this ?

definitions.text: Some swordsmanship we see, in each case ending with this ?

indicators.note: each of the four words before it contributes only its final letter, as the phrase tells the solver

explanation.surface: A fencing display is described, with a teasing hint about how each bout finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of 'Some swordsmanship we see' spell the answer, and the whole clue also defines it: a fencing sword is indeed 'some swordsmanship'.
explanation.definitionFit: The épée is one of the three fencing weapons, so its bouts are a form of swordsmanship.

clue.text: Model for painting by Wright of Derby ?

definitions.text: Model for painting by Wright of Derby ?

parts.words: Model for painting by Wright of Derby ?
parts.note: the eighteenth-century painter Joseph Wright of Derby makes a painting, and a derby is a bowler, a kind of headwear

explanation.surface: Someone sits as a model for a portrait by the English painter Joseph Wright.
explanation.walkthrough: A derby is a bowler, so a 'painting by Wright of Derby' becomes a painting plus headgear. The answer is a wide-brimmed lady's style seen in Gainsborough portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed, often decorated hat of the kind worn in eighteenth-century portraits, a model or style of headwear.

clue.text: Deteriorates or goes badly for part of year

indicators.note: the letters of Deteriorates go awry, and with those of the word or they make the full pool

explanation.surface: Something worsens or fares poorly through part of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the letters of 'Deteriorates' are those of the answer plus O and R from 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastertide is the season around Easter, a period of the church calendar.

clue.text: Police ordered data on swindles

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: cons are confidence tricks, swindles
tables are data set out in order, rows and columns

explanation.surface: Officers sort through records about fraud cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Constables are the ordinary officers who make up a police force.

clue.text: Winners in court case, oddly

indicators.note: the word case is treated oddly, its letters arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: Someone wins in a legal case in a strange manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal but is a tennis court; 'oddly' wants to mean odd letters, but those of 'court case' give nothing, so it is an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an unreturnable serve wins the point, so these serves are point-winners on court.

clue.text: A seat in the Lords

parts.note: a seat is both a padded sofa and a place in the upper house; an earl takes his seat there under the title of a Derbyshire town

explanation.surface: A peer takes his place in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is Britain's upper chamber. The answer is a buttoned leather sofa, and also the earldom whose holder sits in the Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep buttoned sofa bears the name of the earls of Chesterfield, peers entitled to sit in the upper chamber.

clue.text: Oxford colleges responsible for pilot schemes

definitions.meaning: Trinity is one Oxford college, and Christ Church is known there simply as the House
the London corporation that licenses maritime pilots and runs lighthouses

explanation.surface: Two Oxford colleges are said to be in charge of trial projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot schemes' sounds like trial runs, but means arrangements for ships' pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: The corporation of that name in England licenses ship pilots; its two words are names of Oxford colleges.

clue.text: Got the measure of a bore many a Liberal considered joining

definitions.text: Got the measure of a bore

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
rated means considered or judged

explanation.surface: A tedious person was assessed, and plenty of Liberals were thought to be thinking of signing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tiresome person; it is the inner width of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To calibrate a gun is to measure the width of its barrel, its bore or calibre.

clue.text: Mathematician wants graph, say, to change

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it are changed, put in a new order

explanation.surface: A mathematician wishes, perhaps, to alter a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythagoras was the ancient Greek mathematician of the right-angled triangle theorem.

clue.text: Change is by Asian or African country

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are changed, rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A traveller is asked to switch from an Asian nation to an African one.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the old name of Ethiopia, a country in Africa.

clue.text: Prison specified? Given a nominal alternative

parts.note: nick is British slang for a prison or police station
named means specified or identified

explanation.surface: A jail is identified, and someone is offered a token option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nominal' sounds like token or trifling, but means to do with names.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is an alternative name, so being nicknamed is being given one.

clue.text: Pamphlet that gets blanket coverage

definitions.meaning: a single printed page or broadsheet, a small publication
on a bed the linen layer lies under the blanket, so it is covered by it

explanation.surface: A leaflet is said to be distributed everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blanket coverage' suggests mass distribution, but it is literal: the bed linen lies under the blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a printed leaflet or news-sheet, and the bed linen that sits beneath the blanket.

clue.text: Orchid's endless variety-divine flower

indicators.note: a variety of the letters, a different arrangement of them
the word loses its final letter, having no end

parts.note: the flower name is taken as written

explanation.surface: An orchid of unending variation is praised as a heavenly bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ORCHID to ORCHI, and 'variety' rearranges those letters. 'flower' reads as a bloom but means something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor is the fluid flowing in the veins of the gods, a divine liquid that flows.

clue.text: As it's about even, can Democrat, leader become President ?

indicators.note: the tin goes round the other word, being about it

parts.note: taken as written
level means even, flat or equal

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word Democrat

explanation.surface: A Democratic candidate's chances are weighed as the race looks close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LEVEL inside CAN to give CLEVELAN, and the leader of 'Democrat' adds D.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland was a US president, a Democrat who served two separate terms.

clue.text: Joined political groups like a shot?

definitions.meaning: the two wings of politics, put together with hyphens
in game shooting, two barrels fired in quick succession, each hitting a bird

explanation.surface: Someone signed up to political parties without a moment's hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a shot' looks like 'immediately'; in fact it describes a kind of shot in game shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the two wings of politics joined and a double shot that brings down a bird with each barrel.

clue.text: Eastern holy man's double-headed animal

indicators.note: the word gets two heads: its first letter is doubled

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk of Tibet

explanation.surface: An Asian monk owns a two-headed creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double-headed' doubles the first letter of LAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American pack animal of the camel family.

clue.text: That is alternating with very noisy: instrument

indicators.note: the two pairs of letters are woven together so that they alternate, one from each in turn

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Something is said to switch between quiet and very loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternating with' interleaves FF and IE, so the second F moves between I and E. The printed answer LIFE is a typo: the wordplay and definition give a small flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A fife is a small high-pitched flute played in military bands.

clue.text: A left and a right wing so described

explanation.surface: One left-wing and one right-wing figure are characterised in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' and 'right' suggest political wings, but give only L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Alar is the adjective meaning relating to wings, how a wing would be described.

clue.text: Rent from either side of town

indicators.note: the two outer letters stand on each side of the other piece
the letters are taken from the outside of the word town

parts.note: either pairs with or, so it gives that word

explanation.surface: Lodgings to let are found on both edges of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money for lodgings, but it is the past participle meaning ripped. The first and last letters of 'town' go round OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as a past participle means ripped apart, the same as torn.

clue.text: No matter how we describe it, it is not relevant

definitions.text: No matter how we describe it
definitions.meaning: something having no matter, not made of physical substance
of no importance to the point at hand

explanation.surface: However it is put, the speaker insists the point is beside the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both incorporeal, having no physical substance, and unimportant or irrelevant.

clue.text: Rush start of telegram in code

definitions.meaning: in Morse code the letter T, first of telegram, is a single long signal

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to send off the first part of a coded telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: In Morse code the letter T is sent as one long stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry is to race; and Morse's long stroke is the code for T, the first letter of telegram.

clue.text: How pleasant to know these two kings?

parts.note: Edward is the name of several English kings
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how nice it would be to meet a couple of monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear's own comic verse opens 'How pleasant to know Mr Lear!', which the definition quotes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian nonsense poet wrote a self-portrait in verse beginning with these very words.
